question.text: The equations of three waves are given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mi>sin</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>ω</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mi>sin</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>ω</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>  and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mi>cos</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>ω</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>.  Theses waves are in the same direction and are superimposed.  The phase difference between the resultant-wave and the first wave is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>, then what is the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math>?

solution.text:
tanπ4=BCAC=A0(4+32sinϕ)A0(1+32cosϕ)

⇒cosϕ-sinϕ=12
Squaring both sides, ⇒cos2ϕ+sin2ϕ-2cosϕsinϕ=12
⇒2sinϕcosϕ=12
⇒sin2ϕ=12
